plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates a hash table T that uses chaining to resolve collisions, showing the complete mapping from the universe of keys to table slots and their linked-list chains. On the left, two concentric circles represent the key space: the outer dark gray ring is the universe U of all possible keys and the inner light circle is the set K of actual keys stored in the table; eight actual keys k₁ through k₈ are marked as filled black dots within K. The center of the figure shows the hash table T as a vertical column of slots; empty slots are indicated by diagonal hatching, while non-empty slots are white rectangles with arrows pointing right to their chains. On the right, four doubly linked list chains hang off the non-empty slots of T: the first chain contains k₁ and k₄, the second chain contains k₅, k₂, and k₇, the third chain contains k₃ alone, and the fourth chain contains k₈ and k₆. Each list node is drawn as a three-cell box with a left-pointer cell, a key-label cell, and a right-pointer cell; null pointers are indicated by a diagonal slash. Arrows from the keys in K cross to the corresponding slot in T, making the hash function h visible as the mapping that sends multiple keys to the same slot when a collision occurs. This figure introduces chaining as a collision resolution strategy, showing how h partitions the actual keys into groups that share a slot, each group stored as a doubly linked list.

interactionPlan.concept: A hash function h maps each actual key to a slot of table T, and when several keys collide they are simply strung together in that slot's doubly linked list — so the choice of h alone decides how evenly the keys spread and how long the chains get.
elements: Large outer ellipse filled medium gray, label 'U' (universe of keys) set large near its upper edge
Inner ellipse filled light gray nested in U, label 'K' (actual keys) set large at its left edge
Eight filled black key dots inside K, italic labels k₁…k₈ placed beside each dot with offsets chosen so no label overlaps a mapping arrow or a neighbouring dot
Vertical column of equal-height slot rectangles forming table T, with a large 'T' label above the top slot
Empty slots: dark-gray fill with a single diagonal NIL slash
Occupied slots: near-white fill with a short horizontal head-pointer stub on the right edge
Straight thin black arrows from each key dot in K to the left edge of its slot in T (the hash function made visible), crossing each other freely
Four doubly linked chains to the right of T, one per occupied slot
Each chain node drawn as a wide, tall three-field box: narrow prev-pointer field, wide center key-label field (k₁, k₄, …), narrow next-pointer field
Long forward next-arrows along the upper link and long backward prev-arrows along the lower link between consecutive nodes, giving a clear double-link look
Diagonal NIL slash in the prev field of each head node and the next field of each tail node
Head arrow from each occupied slot's stub into the first node of its chain
OPTIONAL (annotation toggle only): numeric key values under the dots, slot index digits 0..m-1 at the left edge of T, chain-length counts, and the α = n/m readout beneath T
Small caption: diagonal slash = NIL

interactions.label: Define the hash function and insert every key
interactions.teaches: That the entire chain structure — which slots stay NIL, which hold long lists — is produced by one expression h(k), and that a colliding key is simply prepended to the existing chain

api.does: returns the number of slots in T (set by the table-size slider)
prepends key k to the chain at slot i and draws its arrow from K — the ONLY way to change the figure; errors if i is not an integer in [0, m())
returns how many keys currently sit in slot i (read-only)
attaches your own comment to the current frame

interactions.frame: the whole figure after one op: the arrow just drawn from the current key dot highlighted, the target slot flashing, and that slot's chain redrawn with the new head node
interactions.success_check: every input key appears in exactly one chain, and each key k sits in slot h(k) with 0 <= h(k) < m()

interactions.teaches: Which keys collided: clicking a slot lights up that slot, every key dot and mapping arrow that leads to it, and its whole chain — searching that slot means walking exactly that list

interactions.label: Table size m
interactions.teaches: How the same eight keys redistribute as m changes — a poor m piles keys into few slots and lengthens every chain

interactions.label: Show numeric detail (key values, slot indices, α)
interactions.teaches: Separates the structural idea (keys → slots → chains) from the bookkeeping numbers, which are hidden by default so the diagram stays as clean as the textbook figure

demo_steps.title: The universe and the actual keys
demo_steps.narration: U holds every key that could ever occur; only the handful in K are really stored. T has far fewer slots than |U|, so some keys must share a slot.

demo_steps.title: Run h(k) = k mod m
demo_steps.narration: The code walks the keys and calls insert(k, k % m()). Each mapping arrow is drawn one at a time; when a second key reaches an occupied slot it is prepended in front of the node already there.

demo_steps.title: A collision is just a longer list
demo_steps.narration: One slot ends up with three keys and a three-node doubly linked chain; another holds one; the rest stay NIL. Chaining never rejects a key — it only lengthens a list.

demo_steps.title: Shrink the table
demo_steps.narration: Drop m to 5 and re-run: the same eight keys crowd into fewer slots, chains roughly double and α = n/m jumps — search cost follows chain length, not table size.

demo_steps.title: A bad hash function
demo_steps.narration: Load the buggy version (or write `return 0`): every key funnels into one slot and the table degenerates into a single linked list with Θ(n) search. Fix h and the chains flatten again.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Chaining makes collisions harmless but not free — the hash function is the only thing standing between a table of short constant-time chains and one long linked list.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: LAYOUT FIRST: call setUiLayout to dock the code editor and controls BELOW the drawing; the SVG must span the full canvas width with no side panel. Use a wide viewBox (roughly 3:2) and three left→right bands: (1) the U/K ellipses on the left third, (2) the vertical slot column T in the middle, (3) the four chains on the right half, with enough right-hand room that the longest three-node chain fits without shrinking. Typography: 'U', 'K', 'T' at ≥20 viewBox px bold/italic as in the source; k₁…k₈ and node key labels ≥16 px. No text smaller than 14 px anywhere; the optional numeric detail appears only when the annotations toggle is on. Do NOT draw chain-length badges, '×N' counters, per-slot index digits, or numeric key values by default. Key-dot labels sit clear of the mapping arrows — place k₂, k₇, k₈ above-left of their dots and k₃ below-left so no label crosses an arrow or touches a neighbouring dot. Chain nodes must be visually generous: each node a wide, tall rectangle divided into narrow-prev / wide-center / narrow-next fields (center field at least twice the width of a pointer field), with a clear gap between nodes spanned by a long forward arrow on the upper link and a long backward arrow on the lower link, so the doubly linked structure reads at a glance. Colors: U medium gray, K light gray, empty slots dark gray with a NIL slash, occupied slots near-white, node boxes white with black strokes. Click highlighting tints one slot, its incoming arrows, its key dots and its whole chain in a single accent (orange) while everything else dims to light gray. During code replay the newly inserted head node flashes.

plan.keyInsight: Chaining makes collisions harmless but not free — the hash function is the only thing standing between a table of short constant-time chains and a single long list.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Three-band layout left→right. Left: two concentric ellipses, outer filled medium gray labeled 'U (universe of keys)' at top, inner filled light gray labeled 'K (actual keys)' at left; eight small filled black dots scattered in the inner ellipse, italic subscripted labels k1…k8 placed just left of or below each dot, with the numeric key value shown in small type. Center: a narrow vertical stack of equal-height rectangles forming T, title 'T' above; empty slots filled dark gray with a thin diagonal slash, occupied slots filled near-white with a short horizontal pointer stub; small index numbers 0..m-1 outside the left edge; an α = n/m readout beneath. Thin black straight arrows run from each key dot across to the left edge of its slot, crossing each other freely — crossings are the visual signature of the hash. Right: for each occupied slot, a horizontal chain of three-cell node boxes (light gray fill, black strokes) with the key label centered; forward next-arrows along the top between boxes and backward prev-arrows along the bottom, diagonal slashes marking NIL in the head's prev cell and the tail's next cell. Highlighting a slot on click should tint the slot, its arrows, its key dots in K, and its whole chain in a single accent color (e.g. orange) while everything else dims. Newly inserted nodes flash at the head of the chain during code replay.

discrepancies: The whole diagram is rendered into roughly the left half of the frame (the UI panel occupies the right half), so the SVG scales to ~1/3 size and nearly every label (U, K, k₁…k₈, T, node keys) becomes too small to read at inline size — in the source these are the dominant, clearly legible annotations.

Extra annotations not in the source clutter the artwork: numeric key values (11, 25, …) printed under each dot at ~7.5px, slot index numbers inside every table slot, a '×N' chain-length tag after each chain, an 'α = n/m' footer and a 'slash = NIL · dark slot = empty' legend.

Chain node proportions differ: source nodes are wide three-field boxes with the key in a large italic centre field and generous slashes; the generated nodes are short/squat with very small key text, and the inter-node forward/backward pointer arrows are thinner and much shorter than the source's long horizontal double links.
Key-dot labels sit very close to the dots and to the fan of mapping arrows in the crowded centre of K (k₂/k₇/k₈ region), producing near-collisions that the source avoids with wider spacing.

Slot fill for occupied slots is a very light gray with an added index digit; source uses uniform light-gray occupied slots with only the pointer stub, giving a cleaner contrast between dark (NIL) and light (occupied) rows.
evaluation.notes: Structurally a faithful reproduction of CLRS hashing-with-chaining (correct slot occupancy, chain contents and order, NIL slashes, doubly linked nodes) with an unusually rich and functional interaction set (demo steps, table-size slider, editable key list, sandboxed hash-function editor with frame-by-frame playback), but the diagram is squeezed into half the frame so nearly all text is illegible at inline size, and several non-source annotations add clutter.
action_items: Call setUiLayout(...) to dock the control panel below (or make it collapsible) so the SVG uses the full width, and raise base font sizes (U/K/T ≥ 20 viewBox px, key labels ≥ 16) so all labels are comfortably readable at inline size.

Remove or make optional the low-value extra text — the 7.5px numeric key values under the dots, the '×N' chain counters, and the per-slot index digits — keeping only the source's k₁…k₈, U, K and T labels by default.
Widen and heighten the chain nodes and lengthen the forward/backward pointer arrows between them to match the source's three-field node proportions and clear double-link look.
Nudge key-dot label offsets (especially k₂, k₇, k₈, k₃) so text does not sit on the mapping arrows or adjacent dots.
plan_action_items: Plan the layout so the figure occupies the full canvas width with the UI docked below; the current side-panel plan structurally guarantees an unreadably small diagram.

feedback.rationale: The critic's core issue is structural — the side-docked UI panel layout planned for the figure guarantees an unreadably small diagram, so the plan must be revised to dock controls below and use full canvas width (plus trim planned extra annotations) before implementation polish matters.

discrepancies: Key-dot layout is compressed: in the source the eight dots are well spread across K (k1 high-left, k6 low-left, k3 at the right edge), whereas the generated dots cluster in a narrow central band so labels k4/k5/k7 and k2/k8/k3 sit almost on top of one another and on neighbouring dots.
The 'K (actual keys)' block label overlaps the inner ellipse boundary and crowds the k1/k2/k6 dots; in the source it sits cleanly in the empty left part of K.

Chain node proportions differ: source nodes are wide three-cell records with generous prev/key/next cells, while the generated nodes are narrow and short, making the internal cell dividers and the prev/next slashes hard to read at inline size.
Added elements not in the source: a 'diagonal slash = NIL' legend line and (when annotations are on) slot indices / α text — minor but extra chrome.

Mapping arrows in the generated figure are thinner and converge at slightly different anchor points than the source's distinct arrowheads stacked at each occupied slot, slightly reducing the 'many keys → one slot' visual emphasis.
evaluation.notes: A faithful and conceptually correct reconstruction of the CLRS chaining figure with an unusually rich and functional interaction set (demo steps, table-size slider, editable key list, sandboxed hash-function workbench with frame playback), but the key dots inside K are clustered so their subscripted labels collide with each other, with the K caption, and with nearby dots, and chain nodes are drawn small relative to the source.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; remaining issues are implementation-level layout and labeling fixes (spread the key dots, reposition the K caption, enlarge chain node cells, thicken mapping arrows).

Diagonal NIL slash in the prev field of each head node and the next field of each tail node

interactions.label: Define the hash function and insert every key
interactions.teaches: That the entire chain structure — which slots stay NIL, which hold long lists — is produced by one expression h(k), and that a colliding key is simply prepended to the existing chain

api.does: returns the number of slots in T (set by the table-size slider)
prepends key k to the chain at slot i and draws its arrow from K — the ONLY way to change the figure; errors if i is not an integer in [0, m())
returns how many keys currently sit in slot i (read-only)
attaches your own comment to the current frame

interactions.frame: the whole figure after one op: the arrow just drawn from the current key dot highlighted, the target slot flashing, and that slot's chain redrawn with the new head node
interactions.success_check: every input key appears in exactly one chain, and each key k sits in slot h(k) with 0 <= h(k) < m()

interactions.teaches: Which keys collided: clicking a slot lights up that slot, every key dot and mapping arrow that leads to it, and its whole chain — searching that slot means walking exactly that list

interactions.label: Table size m
interactions.teaches: How the same eight keys redistribute as m changes — a poor m piles keys into few slots and lengthens every chain

interactions.label: Show numeric detail (key values, slot indices, α)
interactions.teaches: Separates the structural idea (keys → slots → chains) from the bookkeeping numbers, which are hidden by default so the diagram stays as clean as the textbook figure

demo_steps.title: The universe and the actual keys
demo_steps.narration: U holds every key that could ever occur; only the handful in K are really stored. T has far fewer slots than |U|, so some keys must share a slot.

demo_steps.title: Run h(k) = k mod m
demo_steps.narration: The code walks the keys and calls insert(k, k % m()). Each mapping arrow is drawn one at a time; when a second key reaches an occupied slot it is prepended in front of the node already there.

demo_steps.title: A collision is just a longer list
demo_steps.narration: One slot ends up with three keys and a three-node doubly linked chain; another holds one; the rest stay NIL. Chaining never rejects a key — it only lengthens a list.

demo_steps.title: Shrink the table
demo_steps.narration: Drop m to 5 and re-run: the same eight keys crowd into fewer slots, chains roughly double and α = n/m jumps — search cost follows chain length, not table size.

demo_steps.title: A bad hash function
demo_steps.narration: Load the buggy version (or write `return 0`): every key funnels into one slot and the table degenerates into a single linked list with Θ(n) search. Fix h and the chains flatten again.

plan.keyInsight: Chaining makes collisions harmless but not free — the hash function is the only thing standing between a table of short constant-time chains and one long linked list.
plan.reconstructionNotes: LAYOUT FIRST: call setUiLayout to dock the code editor and controls BELOW the drawing; the SVG must span the full canvas width with no side panel. Use a wide viewBox (roughly 3:2) and three left→right bands: (1) the U/K ellipses on the left third, (2) the vertical slot column T in the middle, (3) the four chains on the right half, with enough right-hand room that the longest three-node chain fits without shrinking. Typography: 'U', 'K', 'T' at ≥20 viewBox px bold/italic as in the source; k₁…k₈ and node key labels ≥16 px. No text smaller than 14 px anywhere; the optional numeric detail appears only when the annotations toggle is on. Do NOT draw chain-length badges, '×N' counters, per-slot index digits, or numeric key values by default. Key-dot labels sit clear of the mapping arrows — place k₂, k₇, k₈ above-left of their dots and k₃ below-left so no label crosses an arrow or touches a neighbouring dot. Chain nodes must be visually generous: each node a wide, tall rectangle divided into narrow-prev / wide-center / narrow-next fields (center field at least twice the width of a pointer field), with a clear gap between nodes spanned by a long forward arrow on the upper link and a long backward arrow on the lower link, so the doubly linked structure reads at a glance. Colors: U medium gray, K light gray, empty slots dark gray with a NIL slash, occupied slots near-white, node boxes white with black strokes. Click highlighting tints one slot, its incoming arrows, its key dots and its whole chain in a single accent (orange) while everything else dims to light gray. During code replay the newly inserted head node flashes.

evaluation.notes: A highly faithful reproduction of the CLRS chaining figure — correct 10-slot table with the same occupied/NIL pattern, matching chain contents and order, correct two-ellipse universe and mapping arrows — backed by an unusually rich and pedagogically apt interaction set (step player, m slider, editable key list, sandboxed hash-function workbench with replay); the main weaknesses are the K caption drifting outside the inner ellipse, cramped small key labels, and shrunken chain nodes with stubby pointer arrows.
